correctness.rationale: For n=bq+r the floor differs from arq+c_r by aqn, and multiplying the reduced second gcd argument by b gives ar n-t_r. When t_r>0 every shared prime divides t_r. For a prime dividing b, shared divisibility occurs exactly when the prime divides both r and c_r; otherwise a prime dividing t_r forbids just one q class. CRT gives weight w_r and a period bQ, not necessarily the least. When t_r=0, b divides n². Write n=gm, b=gh, g=gcd(n,b), so gcd(m,h)=1, h divides g, and g=hj. Then gcd(n,an²/b)=jm because h divides b and is coprime to am. It equals one exactly when j=m=1, i.e. n²=b. The r=0 fibers give no hits for b>=6. A putative period starting at or before d=sqrt(b) is a global period for H because it agrees with H on a tail and H is already periodic; it therefore cannot repeat the isolated spike. CRT yields the density, and the remainder of an incomplete period plus the spike yields the stated real-X error. For a'≡au² mod b match r≡ur' mod b: t=t', and c'−c=mr'²−2aukr'−abk² when a'=au²+bm, r=ur'+bk. This vanishes modulo each prime dividing both b and r, so admissibility and the weights match. Independent finite diagnostics (python3 /workspace/branches/independent-reproduction/arithmetic_review.py) made 207600 raw floor/gcd checks across ten mixed denominators including squares and numerators above b, and recovered 1/2 and 23/30 at b=6. They corroborate but do not replace the uniform argument. Frozen checker inspected, not run.
